release_notes: Local offers hosted on the tracker could accept a lead and then answer the buyer with a 404. An uploaded offer is served inline at the campaign URL, so the browser resolved the LeadForge form's action="order.php" against the domain root and posted to /order.php — a path nginx claimed first (snippets/fastcgi-php.conf ends in try_files $fastcgi_script_name =404), so the web server answered with its own 404 and index.php's order bridge never ran. The generated vhost and install.sh's baseline now hand /order.php, /offers/<id>/*.php and /lander/<slug>/*.php to the front controller; AN EXISTING SERVER NEEDS `sudo php /var/www/orbitra/cli/nginx_sync.php` ONCE, because half of this fix lives in the nginx config. success.php joins order.php, thank_you.php, send.php, lucky.php and lemon.php in one shared handler list, so order.php's relative Location redirect no longer dead-ends after the lead was already sent; api.php is honoured only on the routes that carry the bundle's id, never at the domain root where it is the tracker's own admin API. A served offer's relative *.php form actions are rewritten to /offers/<id>/..., so the lead POST carries the offer id instead of depending on a cookie or Referer surviving — in-page anchors and assets are untouched. Uploaded PHP is no longer executable straight off disk: both bundle routes go through index.php under the "Allow PHP landings" switch and its execution budget, and /landings/<id>/*.php returns 404. ORBITRA_OFFER_ID / ORBITRA_OFFER_URL / ORBITRA_OFFER_PATH are defined before a local offer's own PHP runs so a bundle can build an absolute URL for itself and still work standalone.
